texts.facts: This appeal is filed by the appellant U/s.29 of Prevention of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (herein after referred to as the "Act"). 2. The appellant is the petitioner and respondents are husband and parents-in-law and sister-in-law of the petitioner in Crl. Misc. No. 615/2010 on the file of MMTC-1, Bengaluru. Herein afterwards, the parties will be referred to as per their ranks assigned to them before the lower court. 3. Brief facts leading to this appeal are as follows: The marriage between the petitioner and respondent no.1 was solemnized in accordance with Hindu rites and rituals on 29.01.2001. The Nuptial was arranged on the date of marriage at the residence of the petitioner at No.11, Someshwara temple street, Ulsoor, Bengaluru. On the very first night, the respondent no.1 declined to spend time and co-habit with her on the pretext of having high fever. On the next day also, the respondent no.1 refused to co- habit with the petitioner. After 2 days of the marriage, the respondents prepared to leave Bengaluru to Purucherry on 31.01.2001 without taking the petitioner with them and after a great deal of persuasion, agreed to take her along with him. After reaching Puducherry, the respondent no.1 did not stay with her or spend time with her and he maintained distance with her and treated as a complete stranger and she was made to stay away and sleep separately along with his parents. The petitioner stayed for about 20 days at Puducherry from 1.11.2001 to 20.11.2001. During these days, the respondent No.1 stayed away from the petitioner. After 20 days, while the petitioner was returning to Bengaluru, the respondents specifically instructed that she should return Puducherry only after obtaining transfer of her employment. Further she was instructed not even to visit Puducherry for any short visit and she returned back to Bengaluru and reported for duty and her relation with respondent no.1 remained unconsummated. Thereafter she continued to stay along with her parents at Bengaluru. After she returned to Bengaluru, the respondent no.1 severed all sort R.Vanitha vs ) A.Radhakrishnan on 5 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183073143/ 2 of communication from his end, though she tried to contact with respondent no.1 with great difficulty over phone. The respondents did not enquire about her willingness or wellness. Thereafter respondent no.1 was transferred to Cuddalore during the month of June 2002. Respondent no.1 never intimated this aspect to the petitioner. When she enquired with respondent no.1, he had informed her that his deputation to Cuddalore was for a short period and that he would get permanent transfer to Puducherry. Respondent no.1 further assured that till such time she had to stay at Bengaluru with her parents. On believing the version of respondent no.1 and as advised by him, she initiated the process of seeking her transfer to Puducherry and accordingly, she submitted her application on 27.01.2013 for expediting her transfer to Puducherry. In the meanwhile, she learnt that the respondent no.1 had been transferred to Punganur, Andhra Pradesh. Being frustrated about this deliberate act of the respondent on 23.08.2004, she along with her parents went to Punganur and met respondent no.1 at his bank. Respondent no.1 asked her to wait till he seeks transfer to Puducherry. On 4.4.2005, her transfer orders were issued and she was posted to Thindivanam Head Post Office within the jurisdiction of Puducherry division. Though the complainant reported for her duty at Thindivanam which was just one hour journey by road from the matrimonial home at Puducherry, the parents-in-law of the petitioner refused to accommodate her in their house. It was also told that the respondent no.1 not being at home since his transfer orders have not been issued, it was not appropriate for them to keep her at the matrimonial house. The petitioner finding no other alternate had to make her own arrangements and accordingly, took admission in a working women hostel at No. 84, Sundaramastry street, Kosapalyam, Puducherry and started staying there. In the meanwhile, the respondent no.1 was transferred from Punganur to Proddadur in A.P. on 4.9.2007 which was not informed to the petitioner. She met the respondent no.1 at Prodaddur and again pleaded him to set up the matrimonial home at Proddadur and to lead a married life. After the petitioner came to know the transfer of respondent no.1 to Puducherry, she called her parents to Puducherry who immediately joined her and thereafter they went to the residence of respondent no.1 and enquired about the next course of action for resuming her married life. The respondents further gained three months time on the reason of constructing an additional accommodation on the first floor of the residential house of respondent no.1 and the petitioner could join the respondent no.1 thereafter. It was further instructed that till such time, she should continue staying at the working women hostel. Thereafter it was only on 6.2.2009, she was allowed to enter the newly constructed portion of the matrimonial home. The parents of the petitioner furnished the house with all household utensils, almirah, cot, bet, water purifier, stove etc. On the next day of she entering her marital house, the respondents on the pretext of safety, took all the jewelleries weighing about 136 grams of gold and silver items weighing totally about 870 grams of silver belonging to the complainant promising to keep the same in the safe custody of the bank locker. The petitioner on return from her office, she was forced to confine herself to the first floor. As soon as she entering the first floor, the respondents used to lock the gate which was provided in the first floor from outside and the said gate was opened only in the morning 8 a.m making no room even to mingle with her neighbouring family members. The respondent no.1 continued to stay with his parents in the ground floor along with his sister and daughter of his sister. It is further alleged that ever since the petitioner started staying at the residence of respondent no.1, he insisted and received a sum of Rs.10,000/- every from her out of her net salary of Rs. 13,000/-. The respondent no.1 thus collected a total sum of Rs. 1,36,000/- from the petitioner and in the month of March 2009 demanded further sum of Rs. 60,000/- on the pretext of payment of income tax and parents R.Vanitha vs ) A.Radhakrishnan on 5 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183073143/ 3 of the respondent No.1 requested her to arrange a sum of Rs. 50,000/- for purchasing colour TV, washing machine, refrigerator and wet grinder. She has further contended that she had expressed her intention of returning to Bengaluru. At that time, the respondent 1 threatened that she would not be allowed to leave the matrimonial home. Thereafter, she had informed her parents, who immediately rushed to Puducherry on 5.6.2010 and the petitioner and her parents went to All Women police station in Puducherry and lodged a complaint seeking for their protection enabling her to leave Puducherry and come to Bengaluru. The petitioner and her parents being highly apprehensive of the safety of the petitioner left Puducherry who had stayed in Hotel Danaa Orchid, at Puducherry and returned to Bengaluru on the next day. The respondents have deliberately exerted all unbearable cruelty on the petitioner and with deliberate intention of coercing her to meet their illegal and endless greed. The marriage of the petitioner has not consummated even as on that day and her life deliberately ruined by respondent no.1 and his parents. Hence, prayed for allowing the petition. 4. The lower court called for the domestic incident report and issued notice to the respondents. The lower court has no jurisdiction to try the petition. 5. Before the lower court, the petitioner herself examined as P.w.1 and got marked Ex.P1 to 133. The respondent no.1 himself examined as R.w.1 and two independent witnesses have been examined as R.w.2 and 3 and got marked Ex.R1 to R8. After hearing the learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent, the lower court passed an order dismissing the petition filed by the petitioner. 7. After filing of this petition, this court issued notice to the respondent. The respondent has appeared before this court through his counsel and this court secured the lower court records. 8. The appellant has filed an application u/s 28 of Prevention of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 and produced 3 documents and prayed for receiving the said documents as additional documents. Documents sought to be produced are records pertaining to M.C. 2496/2010 and those documents are necessary documents for proper adjudication of the appeal and to determine the question and hence, prayed for allowing the application. The respondent has not filed any objection to the application. . REASONS 12. Point No.1 : The petitioner has filed this appeal challenging the order passed by the lower court in Crl. Misc. No. 615/2010 dismissing the petition filed by the present appellant. At the time of filing this appeal, she has produced 3 documents and prayed for permitting her to produce the said documents as additional documents. Since the documents are certified copies of court record, there is no impediment for this court to receive the documents as additional documents in the above case and hence, I answer point no.1 in the affirmative. 13. Point Nos. 2 to 4 : The petitioner filed petition u/s 12 of Prevention of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 before the lower court which was numbered as C.Misc.615/2010. In the said petition, she has sought various reliefs which reads as follows: (a) Protection order against the respondents under section 18 of the Act prohibiting the respondents from committing any act of domestic violence as against the complainant. (b) Protection from the respondents attempting to threaten the life of the complainant. (c) Protection from the respondents exerting cruelty with ulterior intention of extracting money and property. (g) Directing the respondents to return Rs.1.96 lakhs demanded and taken by the respondent No.1 from the salary of the petitioner and from the parents of the petitioner. R.Vanitha vs ) A.Radhakrishnan on 5 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183073143/ 7 (k) To pay Rs. 50,000/- towards reimbursement of cost, expenses and incidental charges and legal expenses.
texts.arguments: The respondent no.1 has filed his objection and in his objection, he has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts. The fabricated version of the petitioner just to put pressure on the respondent no.1 to yield to the demands of the petitioner and her father. He has denied all the allegations made in the complaint. He has denied that the petitioner is residing at Bengaluru. The petitioner has gained employment as postal Asst. at Head Post Office, Puducherry. He has contended that it was the petitioner who at the very first night of the marriage disclosed to the respondent no.1 that she was suffering from some gynecological problems and was unable to perform conjugal duties and emotionally forced him to give a promise that he will not going to disclose the physical weakness suffering by her to anybody. The respondent no.1 has sacrificed his want of pleasure by not insisting upon the petitioner to perform her conjugal duties just to ensure her that he is not going to force her either psychologically or physically without her willingness to cooperate. Even on several occasions, the respondent no.1 requested the petitioner to go for a thorough medical check up so as to diagnose that what is the physical problem she was really facing. But the petitioner blatantly refused to undergo any medical check up and treatment. The petitioner was never denied permission to go to her parent's house and he never expressed his unwillingness to take the petitioner whenever wanted to go. He has denied that the petitioner got her transfer from Bengaluru to Thindivanam a near place to Pondicherry as per the instructions of the respondents and if these allegations were true, then she had no impediment in applying for a transfer even as early as 2001 immediately after the marriage. He has denied that the petitioner was prevented from entering the matrimonial house. He has denied that the petitioner was living in a hostel at Puducherry while she was serving at Thindivanam. She started living in a hostel at Puducherry much against the wishes of the respondent no.1 just for the reason that she might have to take care of respondent No.2 and 3 who are aged 83 and 70 years old respectively. The respondent No.3 is suffering a rare ailment of the bone which has rendered her almost immobile and requires an attendant always even for the personal needs. The respondent No.4 was the one who was taking care of the respondent No.3 as well as the household chores and the petitioner would not be required to do anything for the family of the respondent No.1. He has further denied that the petitioner was made to stay alone on the first floor and in fact the first floor of the matrimonial home belongs to one Shivasubramanian, the younger brother of respondent no.1. R.Vanitha vs ) A.Radhakrishnan on 5 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183073143/ 4 He has contended that no money was given by the petitioner from her salary to him and he never asked for the same and he was paying the monthly conveyance autorickshaw charges to the petitioner and there was no reason for him to demand and accept Rs.10,000/- monthly from the petitioner. He has denied the demand made by them during the time of marriage. He has further contended that the expenses for the wedding were borne out by them and their family as per their custom prevailed and in fact the first respondent and his brother had taken a loan to meet the wedding expenses. The actual reason for non co-habiting was solely due to the petitioner. He has further contended that once the respondent No.1 got transferred to Puducherry in 2008, he requested the petitioner to join him at the matrimonial house which was then only a single storied structure, but upon the insistence of the petitioner that she would stay only in an independent portion, the respondents and his family had no option but to construct a portion on the first floor to meet the demand of the petitioner. He has denied that the petitioner has not taken away all her belongings on 6.6.2010. He has contended that the petitioner has misused process of law and filed this false petition so as to harass him and his family members mentally and physically and hence, prayed for dismissal of the petition. 6. Feeling aggrieved by the impugned order, the petitioner has filed an appeal contending that the impugned order being cryptic without any reason is arbitrary, capricious and illegal and same requires to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. The learned Magistrate has not adverted to various undisputed factual aspect of the matter which categorically establishes the exertion of sexual violence, verbal and emotional and economical violence and dowry related harassment by the respondents to the appellant. Except selectively extracting the facts narrated in the petition, the learned Magistrate has not appreciated and applied judicious mind into the factual aspect of the matter which categorically establishes the violence exerted on the appellant. The very concept of domestic violence has been disregarded by the learned Magistrate. The learned Magistrate has lost sight of the very psychological aspect of the violence which is essential element in promulgation of the special legislation. The learned Magistrate has failed to appreciate the very purpose of the special legislation in that a person who is married for 8 years was not allowed to stay in her matrimonial house despite having made several sacrifices. The learned Magistrate has failed to appreciate that from the inception of the marriage, the respondent no.1 did not cohabit with the appellant. The appellant made a number of attempts to join the respondent no.1 and to lead happy married life. The learned Magistrate has failed to appreciate this extremely insensitive and inhuman behaviour of the respondent no.1 in considering the psychological violence exerted by the respondent no.1. The learned Magistrate failed to appreciate that the appellant herein being determined to lead a matrimonial life had gone to Puducherry and was forced to live in a working women hostel for a period of over four years. The respondent no.1 being completely aware of this had not even paid a visit to her thereby completely neglecting the very existence of the appellant. The learned Magistrate has not taken this crucial aspect of the matter into consideration. The respondent no.1 who was legally, morally and ethically obligated to provide emotional and physical protection to the appellant R.Vanitha vs ) A.Radhakrishnan on 5 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183073143/ 5 had shattered all the hopes of the appellant on account of non consummation of marriage. Hence, prayed for setting aside the impugned order passed by the lower court. In support of this application, the appellant has filed affidavit and contended that her marriage with respondent no.12 has not been consummated owing to impotency of the respondent and she sought for decree of divorce dissolving the marriage on the ground of cruelty in M.C.No. 2496/2010. (e) To provide accommodation suitable to the standard to which the petitioner is accustomed to. It is further contended that she was made to suffer and undergo unbearable hardship, mental agony at the hands of the respondents. 15. The learned counsel for the petitioner has filed written arguments and submitted that the marriage between the petitioner and respondent no.1 was solemnized on 29.1.2001 at Manishadakshari Kalyana mantap, Bengaluru and the marriage expenses were borne by the parents of the petitioner and the parents of the petitioner had given a sum of Rs.10,000/- by way of cash and gold jewellery of 200 grams as demanded and gold chain, necklace, bangles apart from silver items, brass and silk apparels. Ex. P 4 to 12, Ex.P112, 113, 119 to 128 and 132 are evidencing the marriage expenses and gold ornaments and utensils purchased by the parents of the petitioner. He has further submitted that at the time of marriage, the petitioner was working as postal assistant in General Post Office, Bengaluru and petitioner had joined the employment and working from the year 1993 and at that time, respondent no.1 was working as clerk in Indian Bank Neyveli branch, Tamil nadu and petitioner and her parents were given to understand by the respondent that immediately after the marriage, the respondent no.1 would set up a matrimonial home at Pondicherry and petitioner to take a transfer to Pondicherry to lead marital life. He has further submitted that though the marriage between the petitioner and respondent no.1 continued for a period of 9 years till filing the petition, the marriage has not been consummated, the petitioner was put through grave mental psychological and physical harassment, torture and humility by the respondents. He has further submitted that after the marriage, the petitioner and respondent no.1 stayed in Bengaluru for 2 days and respondent no.1 did not co-habit with the petitioner on the pretext of not being well and after 2 days, the respondents prepared to return to Pondicherry, however declined to take the petitioner along with them and this was the first incident of violence against the petitioner. He has further submitted that after a great deal of pursuing the respondent, agreed to take the petitioner to Pondicherry and thus the petitioner went to Pondicherry stayed with the respondents for about 20 days and during the said period also, the petitioner was made to sleep along with the parents of respondent no.1 and respondent no.1 never spent a single moment with the petitioner and respondent no.1 did not show any interest in consummating the marriage. After 20 days, the petitioner was asked by the respondent to stay at Bengaluru and continued her employment and to join them at Pondicherry only after the transfer from Neyveli to Pondicherry and the petitioner was also asked not even to visit the matrimonial home during the holidays. He R.Vanitha vs ) A.Radhakrishnan on 5 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183073143/ 8 has further submitted that the respondent no.1 did not get transfer from Pondicherry as promised and the respondents never informed the petitioner about the transfer of respondent no.1 to Cuddalor between 31.7.2003 to 19.2.2004, Punganur between 20.2.2004 to 5.9.2007 and Proddatur between 6.9.2007 to 26.4.2008. He has further submitted that the petitioner along with her parents had visited these places of work, the respondent no.1 refused to take her. He has further submitted that respondent no.1 deliberately refusing and being reluctant to take responsibility of the marital life and has caused incidence of domestic violence on the petitioner. He has further submitted that the petitioner obtained transfer from Bengaluru to Dindivanam at Pondicherry division and the respondent did not allow her to reside with them at her matrimonial house on the ground that the respondent no.1 was working in Ponganur, therefore, the petitioner had to stay in a working women hostel known as Pondicherry Corporation for Development of Women and Handicapped persons Ltd. from April 2005 to February 2009 and the petitioner was neither involved nor invited for any of the family religious or social functions. He has submitted that the respondent no.1 had got his transfer to Pondicherry and reported for duty at Pondicherry from May 2008 and he had not intimated the same to the petitioner and the respondent no.1 had never paid a visit to the petitioner at her stay at Pondicherry Corporation for Development of Women and Handicapped persons Ltd and thereafter the petitioner joined the respondent no.1 at her matrimonial home only to stay separately in the first floor of the building without having been allowed to mingle with any of the family members and the respondent no.1 continued to live with his parents i.e. respondent no.2 and 3 in the ground floor. He has submitted that the petitioner had to cook herself and in the first instant, the respondents have snatched the cooking gas cylinder and the petitioner having been stopped providing the cooking gas, she was constrained to take electric stove to cook food for herself vide Ex.P114, therefore, the petitioner filed a police complaint at Pondicherry vide Ex.P129. He has further submitted that the petitioner was locked between 6 p.m and 8 am daily by the respondents 2 and 3 on the premise of safety and the respondents deliberately prohibited and restricted the petitioner to have access even to the basic facilities in the house hold which she was legally entitled and all the jewels and salary of the petitioner was taken by the respondents and the respondents had demanded payment of money on the pretext of clearing the income tax and to buy TV, refrigerator and wet grinder and the petitioner complied with the said demand of the respondents through her father by obtaining a D.D. for Rs. 50,000/- at Ex.P115 and Ex.R1 to R6 confirmed the genuinity of the transaction evidencing the payment of Rs.50,000/- by the petitioner through her father. He has further submitted that the petitioner filed a complaint before Women police station at Pondicherry on 5.6.2010 seeking their assistance for her safe custody from Pondicherry to Bengaluru vide Ex.P129 and upon the advise of the police to pursue her remedy in the court, she had to leave Pondicherry along with her parents to Bengaluru and the details of the belongings with the petitioner brought to Bengaluru are evidence in Ex.P116, being a document way bill issued by Southern Roadways Ltd. He has further submitted that the above incident reveals and establishes the sexual violence, verbal and emotional violence, economic violence and dowry related harassment, psychological humiliation and physical and financial torture underwent by the petitioner at the hands of the respondents. He has further submitted that after the marriage normally, a cot with bed, bed spread, pillows and an almirah required to be given to the newly wedded couple, but in this case, the above items were made to produce for the second time also as the earlier purchase were used by the respondents and refused to return to the petitioner when she was allowed to enter her matrimonial home on 6.2.2009. In his written arguments, he has referred R.Vanitha vs ) A.Radhakrishnan on 5 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183073143/ 9 the statement of objections filed by the respondents admitting that the petitioner had brought her jewellery and minimum amount of household articles and no police supervision was made available at the time of vacating the house on 6.6.2010 and he has also referred the evidence of the respondent no.1 filed by way of affidavit dated 15.2.2012 and in the said affidavit, the respondent No.1 admitted that the petitioner had brought her jewellery when she entered her matrimonial house and finally, he has argued that the petitioner is entitled for the reliefs sought in the petition. 16. The learned counsel for the respondent no.1 has argued that against the said order, they have preferred an appeal. The petitioner has contended that due to deprivation of physical intimacy, she suffered mental cruelty at the hands of respondent no.1. for the petitioner has argued that the deprivation of physical intimacy amounts to cruelty and therefore, the petitioner being an aggrieved person can maintain the petition under the provisions of Prevention of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 and there is sexual abuse and economic abuse and further there is an allegation that the respondent no.1 has not returned the household articles and jewels of the petitioner even after the petitioner left the matrimonial home on 6.6.2010. The respondent no.1 has specifically denied each and every allegations made by the petitioner including the cruelty committed by him and demand of money and non return of household articles and jewels. This is a petition filed by the petitioner alleging that there is sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse, economic abuse. So, burden is heavily on the petitioner to prove and establish that the respondent no.1 is having physical infirmity i.e. impotency and thereby the petitioner is deprived of sexual intimacy with the respondent no.1. Except the bare testimony of the petitioner, she has not examined any independent evidence and she has not produced any medical report stating that the respondent no.1 purposefully kept away from her without consummation of marriage due to impotency. 19. It is the case of the petitioner that as per the demand made by the respondent no.1, her father gave Rs.50,000/- by way of D.D.

He has further submitted that after the marriage, the petitioner and respondent no.1 stayed in Bengaluru for 2 days and respondent no.1 did not co-habit with the petitioner on the pretext of not being well and after 2 days, the respondents prepared to return to Pondicherry, however declined to take the petitioner along with them and this was the first incident of violence against the petitioner. He has further submitted that after a great deal of pursuing the respondent, agreed to take the petitioner to Pondicherry and thus the petitioner went to Pondicherry stayed with the respondents for about 20 days and during the said period also, the petitioner was made to sleep along with the parents of respondent no.1 and respondent no.1 never spent a single moment with the petitioner and respondent no.1 did not show any interest in consummating the marriage. After 20 days, the petitioner was asked by the respondent to stay at Bengaluru and continued her employment and to join them at Pondicherry only after the transfer from Neyveli to Pondicherry and the petitioner was also asked not even to visit the matrimonial home during the holidays. He R.Vanitha vs ) A.Radhakrishnan on 5 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183073143/ 8 has further submitted that the respondent no.1 did not get transfer from Pondicherry as promised and the respondents never informed the petitioner about the transfer of respondent no.1 to Cuddalor between 31.7.2003 to 19.2.2004, Punganur between 20.2.2004 to 5.9.2007 and Proddatur between 6.9.2007 to 26.4.2008. He has further submitted that the petitioner along with her parents had visited these places of work, the respondent no.1 refused to take her. He has further submitted that respondent no.1 deliberately refusing and being reluctant to take responsibility of the marital life and has caused incidence of domestic violence on the petitioner. He has further submitted that the petitioner obtained transfer from Bengaluru to Dindivanam at Pondicherry division and the respondent did not allow her to reside with them at her matrimonial house on the ground that the respondent no.1 was working in Ponganur, therefore, the petitioner had to stay in a working women hostel known as Pondicherry Corporation for Development of Women and Handicapped persons Ltd. from April 2005 to February 2009 and the petitioner was neither involved nor invited for any of the family religious or social functions. He has submitted that the respondent no.1 had got his transfer to Pondicherry and reported for duty at Pondicherry from May 2008 and he had not intimated the same to the petitioner and the respondent no.1 had never paid a visit to the petitioner at her stay at Pondicherry Corporation for Development of Women and Handicapped persons Ltd and thereafter the petitioner joined the respondent no.1 at her matrimonial home only to stay separately in the first floor of the building without having been allowed to mingle with any of the family members and the respondent no.1 continued to live with his parents i.e. respondent no.2 and 3 in the ground floor. The petitioner has contended that due to deprivation of physical intimacy, she suffered mental cruelty at the hands of respondent no.1.
texts.respondent_arguments: The respondent no.1 who was legally, morally and ethically obligated to provide emotional and physical protection to the appellant R.Vanitha vs ) A.Radhakrishnan on 5 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183073143/ 5 had shattered all the hopes of the appellant on account of non consummation of marriage. Hence, prayed for setting aside the impugned order passed by the lower court. In support of this application, the appellant has filed affidavit and contended that her marriage with respondent no.12 has not been consummated owing to impotency of the respondent and she sought for decree of divorce dissolving the marriage on the ground of cruelty in M.C.No. 2496/2010. He has submitted that the petitioner had to cook herself and in the first instant, the respondents have snatched the cooking gas cylinder and the petitioner having been stopped providing the cooking gas, she was constrained to take electric stove to cook food for herself vide Ex.P114, therefore, the petitioner filed a police complaint at Pondicherry vide Ex.P129. He has further submitted that the petitioner was locked between 6 p.m and 8 am daily by the respondents 2 and 3 on the premise of safety and the respondents deliberately prohibited and restricted the petitioner to have access even to the basic facilities in the house hold which she was legally entitled and all the jewels and salary of the petitioner was taken by the respondents and the respondents had demanded payment of money on the pretext of clearing the income tax and to buy TV, refrigerator and wet grinder and the petitioner complied with the said demand of the respondents through her father by obtaining a D.D. for Rs. 50,000/- at Ex.P115 and Ex.R1 to R6 confirmed the genuinity of the transaction evidencing the payment of Rs.50,000/- by the petitioner through her father. He has further submitted that the petitioner filed a complaint before Women police station at Pondicherry on 5.6.2010 seeking their assistance for her safe custody from Pondicherry to Bengaluru vide Ex.P129 and upon the advise of the police to pursue her remedy in the court, she had to leave Pondicherry along with her parents to Bengaluru and the details of the belongings with the petitioner brought to Bengaluru are evidence in Ex.P116, being a document way bill issued by Southern Roadways Ltd. He has further submitted that the above incident reveals and establishes the sexual violence, verbal and emotional violence, economic violence and dowry related harassment, psychological humiliation and physical and financial torture underwent by the petitioner at the hands of the respondents. He has further submitted that after the marriage normally, a cot with bed, bed spread, pillows and an almirah required to be given to the newly wedded couple, but in this case, the above items were made to produce for the second time also as the earlier purchase were used by the respondents and refused to return to the petitioner when she was allowed to enter her matrimonial home on 6.2.2009. In his written arguments, he has referred R.Vanitha vs ) A.Radhakrishnan on 5 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183073143/ 9 the statement of objections filed by the respondents admitting that the petitioner had brought her jewellery and minimum amount of household articles and no police supervision was made available at the time of vacating the house on 6.6.2010 and he has also referred the evidence of the respondent no.1 filed by way of affidavit dated 15.2.2012 and in the said affidavit, the respondent No.1 admitted that the petitioner had brought her jewellery when she entered her matrimonial house and finally, he has argued that the petitioner is entitled for the reliefs sought in the petition. 16. The learned counsel for the respondent no.1 has argued that against the said order, they have preferred an appeal. for the petitioner has argued that the deprivation of physical intimacy amounts to cruelty and therefore, the petitioner being an aggrieved person can maintain the petition under the provisions of Prevention of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 and there is sexual abuse and economic abuse and further there is an allegation that the respondent no.1 has not returned the household articles and jewels of the petitioner even after the petitioner left the matrimonial home on 6.6.2010. The respondent no.1 has specifically denied each and every allegations made by the petitioner including the cruelty committed by him and demand of money and non return of household articles and jewels. This is a petition filed by the petitioner alleging that there is sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse, economic abuse. So, burden is heavily on the petitioner to prove and establish that the respondent no.1 is having physical infirmity i.e. impotency and thereby the petitioner is deprived of sexual intimacy with the respondent no.1. Except the bare testimony of the petitioner, she has not examined any independent evidence and she has not produced any medical report stating that the respondent no.1 purposefully kept away from her without consummation of marriage due to impotency. 19. It is the case of the petitioner that as per the demand made by the respondent no.1, her father gave Rs.50,000/- by way of D.D.
